overall.basis: It is set against what has been written down somewhere a reader can check, not against everything that has happened. Three things hold it down. Whole scopes have had no research round yet. Countries whose courts and press do not publish leave almost nothing to find, so the thinnest parts of the map are often the places where the most is going on. And where someone has counted, as in the registers below, a single case on this map usually stands for many episodes underneath it.

registers.name: Italian local administrations dissolved for mafia infiltration
registers.scope: Dissolutions of councils and local health authorities under art. 143 TUEL, 1991 to February 2018
registers.counts: dissolutions (230 distinct bodies once repeats are netted out)
registers.pub: Chamber of Deputies research service, quoting the parliamentary Antimafia Commission's final report
registers.note: an executive finding that a council was conditioned by a mafia, not a criminal conviction

registers.name: Colombian members of Congress found criminally responsible for paramilitary ties
registers.scope: Rulings of the Supreme Court's Criminal Cassation Chamber in the parapolitica proceedings, to 2010
registers.pub: ICTJ, compiling Supreme Court rulings; hosted on the Court's own site
registers.note: 116 members were under investigation and at least 95 investigations were still open
registers.match: Colombian cases naming paramilitaries reaching into office

registers.name: Defendants charged by the US Justice Department over FIFA
registers.scope: People and companies charged in the FIFA racketeering case, to 3 December 2015
registers.pub: US Department of Justice
registers.note: charges, not convictions, and a snapshot: the case continued after 2015
registers.match: cases naming FIFA or a FIFA confederation

registers.name: IOC members who lost their position over the Salt Lake City 2002 bid
registers.scope: Expulsions and resignations following the IOC commission's 1999 report
registers.pub: Olympedia, reporting the commission's recommendations and the IOC Session votes
registers.note: mixes expulsions with resignations; no IOC page carrying a stated total was reachable
registers.match: cases naming the Salt Lake City bid or the IOC

registers.name: Companies paying kickbacks on UN Oil-for-Food contracts
registers.scope: Companies listed in the Independent Inquiry Committee's final report, October 2005
registers.pub: Independent Inquiry Committee into the Oil-for-Food Programme; number read on a law-firm summary of the report
registers.note: humanitarian-goods kickbacks only, not oil surcharges; the inquiry's own pages were unreachable

registers.name: UN staff found to have committed misconduct on Procurement Task Force findings
registers.scope: Staff the UN Administration concluded were involved in misconduct, acting on the Task Force's disciplinary recommendations
registers.pub: UN Board of Auditors, A/63/167
registers.note: seven had been dismissed at the time of the audit; some cases were still on appeal
registers.match: cases naming UN procurement or the Procurement Task Force

registers.name: FCPA enforcement actions
registers.scope: Every action brought by the US Justice Department and the SEC under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act since 1977
registers.pub: Stanford Law School FCPA Clearinghouse
registers.note: one bribery scheme usually produces several actions, so the number of distinct episodes is smaller
registers.match: cases on this map whose source is an FCPA action

registers.name: Concluded foreign bribery cases in the OECD Convention countries
registers.scope: Foreign bribery enforcement actions concluded in the Parties to the Convention between 1999 and 2014
registers.pub: OECD Foreign Bribery Report 2014; figures read on a law-firm commentary, the OECD page being unreachable
registers.note: 27 per cent involved officials of state-owned or state-controlled companies
registers.match: company cases on this map from those years naming bribery

registers.name: Chinese espionage incidents in the United States
registers.scope: Publicly reported instances of espionage directed at the US by China since January 2000
registers.pub: Center for Strategic and International Studies
registers.note: compiled from public reporting, so sealed and unprosecuted cases are absent
registers.match: US cases from 2000 on where a foreign state reached in and China is named

registers.name: Americans convicted of espionage
registers.scope: American citizens convicted of espionage or related offences against the United States, 1947 to 2015
registers.pub: Defense Personnel and Security Research Center, US Department of Defense
registers.note: citizens only: foreign nationals operating inside the US are excluded
registers.match: US cases from those years where a foreign state reached in

registers.name: People prosecuted in Taiwan for spying for China
registers.scope: Prosecutions in Taiwan for espionage on behalf of China, in 2024
registers.pub: Taiwan's National Security Bureau, reported by the Taipei Times
registers.note: 2024 alone; the same report gives 16 for 2021 and 10 for 2022, so there is no multi-year total
registers.match: Taiwanese cases from 2024 where a foreign state reached in

registers.name: West German citizens who spied for East Germany
registers.scope: Sources run inside West Germany by East German intelligence in the late 1980s
registers.pub: Bundesarchiv, Stasi Records Archive
registers.note: the archive's own figure is approximate, and many sources were in industry rather than state bodies

registers.name: Convictions for spying for Russia in Estonia
registers.scope: People convicted by Estonian courts of espionage or treason for Russian services since 2009
registers.pub: International Centre for Defence and Security, Tallinn
registers.note: court verdicts only: recruits expelled, turned or never charged are absent
registers.match: Estonian cases from 2009 on naming a Russian service

registers.name: Espionage investigations opened in Poland
registers.scope: Investigations opened by Poland's Internal Security Agency in 2025
registers.pub: ABW activity report, reported by Notes from Poland
registers.note: investigations, not proven cases; 82 people were charged across 2024 and 2025 together
registers.match: Polish cases from 2024 on where a foreign state reached in

registers.name: Names on the P2 lodge list seized at Castiglion Fibocchi
registers.scope: The single Propaganda Due membership list seized by Milan magistrates in March 1981
registers.pub: Il Post, reporting the seized list and the Anselmi commission's work
registers.note: membership, not a finding of influence: the list held 59 MPs, 119 senior officers, 5 undersecretaries and 1 constitutional judge

registers.name: Police officers in England and Wales who declared freemason membership
registers.scope: Voluntary returns from 26 forces after the Home Affairs Committee inquiry, out of 38,875 returns
registers.pub: UK Home Office, written answer to Parliament
registers.note: declaration was voluntary and covers 26 forces only; no figure was given for judges or magistrates

registers.name: Turkish public officials dismissed by emergency decree after the 2016 coup attempt
registers.scope: People removed from public service by decree, as counted by the commission set up to hear appeals
registers.pub: OHAL Commission annual report, reported by Hurriyet Daily News
registers.note: an executive act, not a finding about any individual: the Venice Commission said the dismissals cited no verifiable evidence per person
registers.match: Turkish cases naming the Gulen movement

registers.name: LDP Diet members reporting dealings with the Unification Church
registers.scope: The Liberal Democratic Party's own survey of its 379 members of the Diet, 2022
registers.pub: The Japan Times, reporting the party's survey
registers.note: self-reported contact, not a finding of influence; only 17 were recorded as taking the church's campaign help
registers.match: Japanese cases naming the Unification Church

registers.name: People and businesses the Zondo commission recommended for prosecution
registers.scope: Prosecution recommendations in the South African state capture inquiry's reports to May 2022
registers.pub: Daily Maverick, tallying the commission's own recommendations
registers.note: the published figure is “just over 130”, so it is a floor; recommendations, not convictions
registers.match: South African cases naming the Guptas or state capture

registers.name: Criminal networks in the EU that use corruption
registers.scope: Europol's list of the 821 most threatening criminal networks in the EU, of which 71 per cent use corruption and 86 per cent misuse legal businesses
registers.pub: Europol
registers.note: a network is not an episode, and there is no way to tell which of the 821 this map carries, so no share is shown; the 2026 refresh lists 731 and must not be added to this
